# Appendix G: Suggested Reading

To continue expanding your computational skills beyond this introductory book, here are highly recommended resources:

## 1. Introductory Programming
- **Python Crash Course (3rd Edition, Eric Matthes, No Starch Press):** A hands-on, project-based introduction to general-purpose Python.
- **Think Python: How to Think Like a Computer Scientist (3rd Edition, Allen B. Downey, O'Reilly):** An exceptional conceptual guide that teaches computer science thinking and algorithm design.

## 2. Scientific Python Ecosystem
- **Official NumPy Documentation & User Guide (`https://numpy.org/doc/`):** Comprehensive tutorials on broadcasting, indexing, and vectorization techniques.
- **Official Matplotlib Documentation & Gallery (`https://matplotlib.org/stable/gallery/`):** The gallery contains hundreds of visual examples with source code that you can adapt for your own research papers.
- **Python Data Science Handbook (Jake VanderPlas, O'Reilly):** Detailed coverage of NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, and Scikit-Learn.
- **SciPy Lecture Notes (`https://scipy-lectures.org/`):** Outstanding self-paced tutorials for scientists and engineers.
